q.t: How many does this tally show: one bundle of five (four strokes crossed by a fifth) and 2 more strokes?
q.e: A crossed bundle is 5; add the 2 single strokes.

q.t: The frequency of a value means …
o: where it is in the list
q.e: Frequency = number of times a value turns up in the data.

q.t: Which question needs you to COLLECT data?
o: What is the most popular TV show in my class?
What is the capital of India?
How many days are there in a week?
q.e: Only the first depends on particular people right now; the others are fixed facts you can look up.

q.t: In a pictograph, 1 symbol = 10 students. A row has 4 symbols. How many students?
q.e: Count the symbols and multiply by the key: 4 × 10 = 40.

q.t: In a pictograph, 1 symbol = 10. What does half a symbol stand for?
q.e: Half a symbol is half the key: 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

q.t: In a bar graph, what shows the value of each category?
o: The length (or height) of the bar
q.e: Widths and gaps are kept equal so that only the length carries information.

q.t: Bars in a bar graph should have …
o: the same width and equal gaps
q.e: Equal widths stop a fatter bar from looking bigger than it really is.

q.t: What does the 'key' of a pictograph tell you?
q.e: Without the key you can't turn symbols into numbers.

q.t: Shoe sizes in order: 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7. What is the largest size?
q.e: In ascending order the largest value is at the end.

q.t: Bar graph scale: 1 unit = 100 vehicles. A bar is 12 units tall. How many vehicles?
q.e: Length × scale = 12 × 100 = 1,200.

q.t: Sweets chosen: jalebi 6, barfi 3, gujiya 13, rasgulla 7, gulab jamun 9. How many sweets in all?
q.e: Add the frequencies: 6 + 3 + 13 + 7 + 9 = 38.

q.t: Is that sweets frequency table enough to give each student the sweet they chose?
o: No — it shows how many chose each sweet, not who chose which
Yes — it has all the numbers
Yes — if you add them up
No — it has too many sweets
q.e: Organising into a frequency table loses the names. You'd need the original list.

q.t: 1 kite symbol = 100 kites. Rani bought 300 kites. How many symbols?
q.e: 300 ÷ 100 = 3 symbols.

q.t: Poonam Ben bought 700 kites and Rani 300. Did Poonam buy more than double Rani's?
q.e: Compare with double: 2 × 300 = 600. 700 is more.

q.t: A pictograph key is 1 symbol = 10 students. Which number CAN'T be shown neatly with whole or half symbols?
q.e: 35 = 3½ symbols, but 33 would need 3.3 symbols.

q.t: A bar graph's scale is 1 unit = 5 students. How many units tall is the bar for 45 students?
q.e: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 units.

q.t: 8–9 a.m.: 1,000 vehicles; 9–10 a.m.: 800 vehicles. How many in these two hours together?
q.e: Read each bar and add: 1,000 + 800 = 1,800.

q.t: In an absentee bar graph, one class has NO bar. What does that mean?
o: No one was absent — full attendance
q.e: A bar of length 0 means the value is 0.

q.t: To show the heights of the tallest child in each class, which bars feel most natural?
q.e: Heights are measured upwards, so upward (vertical) bars match the real thing.

q.t: Why do we bundle tally marks in fives?
o: Counting bundles (5, 10, 15…) is faster and harder to get wrong
Because there are 5 days in a school week
q.e: Bundles let you count in fives instead of one stroke at a time.

q.t: Mudhol dogs: A 18, B 36, C 12, D 48, E 18, F 24. With key 1 symbol = 6 dogs, how many symbols for Village B?
q.e: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 symbols. 6 works as a key because every number is a multiple of 6.

q.t: Same data: how many dogs are there in Villages B and D together?
Same data: how many dogs in Villages A, C, E and F together?
q.e: 18 + 12 + 18 + 24 = 72 — so B and D together (84) really do have more.

q.t: A bar 6 units long shows 24 tickets. What is the scale?
q.e: Scale = value ÷ length = 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

q.t: With 1 unit = 4 tickets, how many tickets does a 5-unit bar show?
q.e: Length × scale = 5 × 4 = 20.

q.t: Education costs ₹800 and food ₹3,400. What is one-fourth of the food cost?
q.e: 3,400 ÷ 4 = 850. Since 800 < 850, education is less than a quarter of food.

q.t: A bowler took 3 wickets in each of 8 matches. How many wickets is that?
q.e: Value × frequency: 3 × 8 = 24.

q.t: Runs scored go up to about 100. Which scale is most sensible?
q.e: 1 unit = 10 runs gives a tallest bar of about 10 units — easy to draw. 1 run per unit means 100 marks; 100 runs per unit makes every bar tiny.

q.t: 1 symbol = 4 girls. Class 2 has 4½ symbols. Two more girls join. How does the row change?
o: The half symbol becomes a full symbol (5 symbols)
One more half symbol is added
q.e: 4½ symbols = 18 girls. 18 + 2 = 20 = 5 full symbols.

q.t: Which is best shown with horizontal bars?
q.e: Rivers stretch along the ground, so sideways bars match them.

q.t: Wickets: 0 in 5 matches, 1 in 4 matches, 2 in 3 matches, 3 in 2 matches. Total wickets?
q.e: Multiply each value by its frequency and add: 0 + 4 + 6 + 6 = 16.

q.t: Same data: in how many matches did he bowl in total?
q.e: Add the frequencies (numbers of matches): 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 14.

q.t: Mayank finds a bowler's total wickets by adding 0 + 1 + 2 + … + 7. Why is that wrong?
o: Each value must be multiplied by how many matches it happened in
He should add only the even numbers
q.e: If 3 wickets came in 8 matches, that's 24 wickets, not 3. Total = Σ value × frequency.

q.t: An infographic shows Everest looking about twice as tall as Elbrus (5,642 m). What would twice Elbrus be?
q.e: 5,642 × 2 = 11,284 m — but Everest is 8,848 m, so the picture misleads.

q.t: Mountains drawn as triangles where taller ones are also wider. What's the problem?
o: Width suggests extra information (size) the data doesn't give
q.e: Equal widths keep the comparison to height alone; wider triangles look 'bigger' than the heights justify.

q.t: A survey of 120 students: playing 45, reading 30, painting 20, rest is music. How many chose music?
q.e: The groups add up to the total: 120 − 45 − 30 − 20 = 25.

q.t: Data: 12, 15, 18, 21, 27 (all multiples of 3). Which key gives a pictograph with only whole symbols?
q.e: 3 divides every value exactly, so each row is a whole number of symbols.

q.t: Scale 1 unit = 50 vehicles. A bar reaches 7½ units. How many vehicles?
q.e: 7 × 50 = 350, plus half a unit = 25: 375.

q.t: A class's shoe sizes are put in ascending order. Which question does this make EASIEST to answer?
o: How many students wear sizes larger than 4?
What is each student's favourite game?
q.e: Ordered data puts equal values together and bigger ones after, so you just count from the last 4 onward. Names aren't in the list at all.

q.t: Cars passing a crossing: 6–7 a.m. 250, 7–8 a.m. 1,200, 8–9 a.m. 1,000. How many more cars at 7–8 than at 6–7?
q.e: 1,200 − 250 = 950. The jump makes sense: people leave for school and work.
